title.en: Geography: India - Location, Relief and Drainage

text.en: Asha traced India's shape on a map. "Mountains in the north, sea on three sides," she said.

India lies in the northern and eastern hemispheres between 8 degrees 4 minutes and 37 degrees 6 minutes north latitude. The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle. The Standard Meridian is 82.5 degrees east, which gives Indian Standard Time.
India's physical divisions are the Northern Mountains (Himalayas), the Northern Plains, the Peninsular Plateau, the Indian Desert, the Coastal Plains and the Islands. The Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiris, and Anaimudi is the highest peak in South India.
The Himalayan rivers such as the Ganga, Indus and Brahmaputra are perennial. Peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Krishna and Cauvery are seasonal, and they flow east into the Bay of Bengal, except the Narmada and Tapi, which flow west.
